land.text: the Taurus country around Sis and Vahka, where Ruben 'revolted against Byzantium in 1080'; the page gives no boundary, so the first Cliopatria shape stands for it

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Seljuk Empire, Byzantine Empire under the Doukas dynasty, Bagratid Armenia'.

land.text: Ruben was 'linked to Gagik II' of Bagratid Armenia; the infobox lists it as a predecessor

predecessors.note: A dynastic, not a territorial handover: Bagratid Armenia ended in 1045 (Cliopatria 886-1045) and held no land in Cilicia.

land.text: Adana and Tarsus (1359) and 'the remaining areas of Cilicia' (1375), with Sis falling on 13 April 1375

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Mamluk Sultanate, Kingdom of Cyprus, Jerusalem and Armenia, Ramadanid Emirate'.

land.text: the Ramadanid Turkmen emirate in Cilicia, authorised by the Mamluks; Adana its centre

successors.note: The Mamluks 'authorized Ramazan Beg's Türkmen Emirate to administer Cilicia, but took direct control of the towns of' Tarsus, Ayas, Sarvandikar and Sis (Ramadanids page); the emirate was founded in 1352 and the Cliopatria row starts in 1385.

land.text: title only: the Armenian crown passed to James I of Cyprus in 1396

successors.note: No land; the title was transferred in 1396 after Leo V's death in 1393.

capitals.name: Tarsus
capitals.note: Infobox: Tarsus 1080-1198, Sis 1198-1375; the body says Thoros I 'moved the capital from Tarsus to Sis' around 1100 and Leo I was crowned at Tarsus in 1198. Cliopatria's 1099-1146 shapes do not include Tarsus.

capitals.name: Sis (Kozan)
capitals.note: Taken from the body (Thoros I); sacked and burnt after Mari in 1266; fell to the Mamluks on 13 April 1375. In 1137-1141 the Byzantines held the country.

correction.text: the Rubenid principality in the Taurus around Sis and Vahka; the extent in 1080-1098 is not given by any page, so the first Cliopatria shape is used

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1099 but Ruben 'revolted against Byzantium in 1080' and 'the foundations of the independent Armenian princedom of Cilicia' were laid ('Founded: c. 1080'). Constantine I gained crusader allies in c. 1097-1099. The extent is a bridge at confidence 1.

1099-1110, 20,547 km2, the Taurus around Sis, Vahka and Gaban (the shape holds no plain city). The infobox gives about 40,000 km2 for the 13th century, so this early figure is not comparable; Thoros I's 1112 capture of Cyzistra is not located by the page.

correction.text: the 1111 shape, valid 1111-1128: Levon I, reigning from 1129, integrated the coastal cities

keyframe_review.note: 1111-1138, 20,695 km2. 'Levon I: Integrated the coastal cities, including Adana, Mamistra (Mopsuestia), Ayas and Korikos, into the principality'; the page dates it only by his reign (1129-1137), so the shape stands to 1128 and the next keyframe applies from 1129. Cliopatria's 1111-1146 shapes show no coast at all.

correction.text: the 1111 shape plus the coastal cities Levon I integrated

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the principality with the plain-coast cities Adana, Mamistra, Ayas and Korikos, bridged to Levon I's reign (1129-1137). Confidence 2: the page does not date the integration within the reign.

correction.text: the 1139 shape, valid 1145-1146 only: Thoros II became lord of Armenian Cilicia in 1144/1145 after eight years of Byzantine rule

keyframe_review.note: 1139-1146, 21,731 km2. In 1137 John II took the country and captured Leo I, Roupen and Thoros; 'Cilicia stayed under Byzantine rule for eight years' (Thoros II page); Thoros was freed in 1141 and took Vahka afterwards, becoming lord in 1144/1145. For 1137-1140 there is no Armenian land; 1141-1144 is the next keyframe. [orchestrator 2 Nov 2026: from/to set to 1145..1146 from this entry's own 'valid 1145-1146 only'; without them the compiler drew the shape for all its Cliopatria years, overlapping the next keyframe (window p1100-p1199 report)]

correction.text: Vahka, the first castle Thoros took after his release in 1141 (then Amouda and other places); the rest of Cilicia stayed Byzantine

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the page gives no year for Thoros's first conquests ('Post-1141 (no date given)'), so the shape is a confidence-1 bridge between the 1137 conquest and the lordship of 1144/1145.

correction.text: the 1139 shape (the Taurus core), valid 1147-1150; the plain cities were regained only in 1151

keyframe_review.note: 1147-1151, 41,874 km2, bbox south to 36.2 N and west to 33.6 E: Tarsus, Adana, Mamistra, Anazarbus and Silifke are inside. 'Smbat Sparapet writes that Thoros took Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun from the Romans' in 1151; Tarsus, Adana and Anazarbus are undated. Cliopatria draws the plain four years early.

correction.text: the 1147 shape in 1151, once Thoros had taken Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the single year 1151: the Cilician plain regained. The Cliopatria 1152 shape follows.

1152-1187, 34,348 km2. Sultan Masud 'reached Anazarbus but accomplished nothing' in 1154; in 1157 Thoros surrendered Berdus to Kilij Arslan after his brother Stephen seized Kokison and Berdus; in 1158 Thoros II 'pays homage to Manuel I' in a treaty (Cilicia page). The loss of Berdus is not located, so the shape stands; Mleh ruled from 1170, Roupen III from 1175. The north strip lost against 1147 (to 38.35 N) is unexplained by any page.

1188-1191, 34,460 km2, unchanged. Leo succeeded Roupen III in 1187: 'During 1187, he became the ruler'; he 'actually forced the allied forces to retreat' from Aleppo and Damascus. Bagras was captured in 1191 (next shape).

1192-1201, 59,705 km2, bbox west to 30.6 E: Mut, Ermenek and Marash are now inside. Leo 'conquered Isauria and came as far as Iconium' (undated) and 'doubled its Mediterranean coast' (Cilicia page); the infobox gives about 40,000 km2 for the 13th century (ratio 1.5, within a factor of two). The reach to 30.6 E is not supported by a page; Alanya was held by its governor Kir Fard until Kayqubad I took it in 1221 (Kayqubad I page).

1202-1249, 59,606 km2. Leo seized Amanus fortresses around 1204, entered Antioch on 14 February 1216 and left it in 1219; Kaykaus I captured Armenian forts north of the Taurus in 1216 and 'Leo later lost the strongholds to the Seljuks'. The pages disagree on the west: the Cilicia page has Kayqubad I taking 'regions west of Seleucia' (undated), Kayqubad's campaign of 1225 reduced Cilicia to a vassal state (Kayqubad I page), while the Rum page has Cilicia taking the coast 'from the Seljuk in the 1240s' and the Karamanids page has Karaman Bey's conquests 'mainly at the expense of Lesser Armenia' in the 1240s. The shape stands unverified in the west.

1250-1259, 59,469 km2, unchanged. Hethum I submitted to the Mongols (1244, agreement of 1247 and journey of 1254), fought beside Hulagu at Aleppo and Damascus in 1259-1260 and 'Marash and Behesni were recovered in the 1250s'. Constantine of Lampron, a disloyal vassal who helped the Sultanate of Rum attack in 1245, was executed in 1250 (Hethum I page).

correction.text: the 1260 shape without Mut and Ermenek, valid 1260-1271

keyframe_review.note: 1260-1271, 43,517 km2, bbox 32.6-38.2 E: the far-west coast and the northern castles Gaban and Hajin are out, the east (Hromgla, Aintab) is in. 'c. 1260: Kilij Arslan IV gave Karaman Bey Larende and Ermenek' and the Battle of Mut is dated 1260 (Karamanids page), so Mut and Ermenek are removed. Gaban and Hajin are missing from the shape although the Cilicia page keeps them Armenian to 1375: unverified. The loss of 1266 at Mari ('conceding territory to the Egyptians') is unnamed by the page.

correction.text: the 1272 shape without Mut and Ermenek, valid 1272-1293

keyframe_review.note: 1272-1293, 43,714 km2, unchanged in extent. Tarsus was taken and 15,000 killed in 1275; a ten-year truce in 1285 had Armenia cede fortresses and pay 'one million dirhams a year'; Al-Ashraf Khalil sacked Hromgla in 1292 and the Catholicosate moved to Sis. The pages do not say the Mamluks annexed any of these, so the shape stands apart from Mut and Ermenek.

correction.text: the 1294 shape without Mut and Ermenek, valid 1294-1304

keyframe_review.note: 1294-1304, 43,640 km2. The Mongol-Armenian victory at Wadi al-Khazandar on 23 December 1299 was undone in May 1300; Battle of Homs 30 March 1303 and Shaqhab 21 April 1303. Hromgla stays inside the shape although it was sacked in 1292.

1305-1325, 36,674 km2, bbox west to 33.6 E: Mut and Ermenek are now outside, as the Karamanids page implies from c. 1260. Oshin was crowned at Tarsus after 1307, Bularghu murdered the Armenian party at Anazarbus in 1307.
1326-1343, 36,551 km2, unchanged. Levon IV was assassinated in 1341, Guy de Lusignan anointed in 1342, a Mamluk invasion followed in 1343-1344.

correction.text: the 1344 shape, valid 1344-1358: the Mamluks took Adana and Tarsus in 1359

keyframe_review.note: 1344-1362, 36,575 km2. 'The Mamluk army took over Adana and Tarsus, two major cities of the plain, leaving few castles to the Armenians' in 1359; Cliopatria's smaller shape begins in 1363.

correction.text: the Armenian rump after the Mamluk conquest of Adana and Tarsus in 1359: Sis and the castles

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1363 shape four years earlier.

correction.text: the 1363 shape, valid 1363-1375: Sis fell on 13 April 1375

keyframe_review.note: 1363-1374, 29,383 km2, bbox 34.7-38.2 E. Sis fell on 13 April 1375 and Gaban followed; 'The Mamluks gained control of the remaining areas of Cilicia' in 1375 (Ramadanids page). Only the end year changes. Silifke drops out of the shape between 1344 and 1363; no page dates it.

region.text: the Rubenid princedom in the Taurus

ledger.note: c. 1080: Ruben founds the Armenian princedom of Cilicia. 'Ruben, linked to Gagik II, revolted against Byzantium in 1080 and the foundations of the independent Armenian princedom of Cilicia were laid'; infobox 'Founded: c. 1080 as the Rubenid principality'. The page gives no boundary.
c. 1100: Thoros I moves the capital from Tarsus to Sis. The page says he succeeded 'around 1100' and moved the capital; the infobox has Tarsus to 1198.

region.text: the coastal cities Adana, Mamistra, Ayas and Korikos

ledger.note: 1129-1137: Levon I integrates the coastal cities. 'Levon I: Integrated the coastal cities, including Adana, Mamistra (Mopsuestia), Ayas and Korikos, into the principality'; the page gives only his reign (from 1129) and does not say from whom.

region.text: the 1111 shape plus the coastal cities Levon I integrated

ledger.note: 1137: John II conquers Cilicia. 'Emperor John II took most cities on the Cilician plains. Levon was imprisoned in Constantinople' (died there about 1141); Thoros II page: 'Cilicia stayed under Byzantine rule for eight years'.

After 1141: Thoros, freed from Constantinople, takes Vahka. The page says only 'Post-1141 (no date given)': per Vahram he 'took Vahka and ... first gained Amouda, then other places'; the year is a bridge.

region.text: the Taurus core of the 1139 shape

ledger.note: 1144/1145: Thoros II becomes lord of Armenian Cilicia. The page gives '1144/1145: Thoros became lord of Armenian Cilicia (Rubenid dynasty), reigning until 1169' after eight years of Byzantine rule.

1151: Thoros II takes Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun from the Byzantines. 'Smbat Sparapet writes that Thoros took Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun from the Romans'; Duke Andronicus came with 12,000 cavalry and Thoros breached Mamistra's walls at night.

region.text: the plain cities Tarsus, Adana and Anazarbus and the coast Cliopatria adds in 1147

ledger.note: Page silent: no page opened dates the recovery of Tarsus, Adana and Anazarbus (Adana is named only as a hunting ground); Cliopatria draws them from 1147, the page's Mamistra from 1151.

1191: Leo captures Bagras from Saladin's hands. 'In 1191, Leo captured and restored Bagras, a strategically important fortress previously taken by Saladin' from the Knights Templar; 'Bohemond demanded its return to the Templars, but Leo refused', and in the later peace brokered by Henry II of Champagne (undated on the page) 'Leo's control of Bagras was confirmed'. Counterpart corrected from the Templars to the Ayyubids by reviewer me-09-b.

region.text: Isauria, with Mut, Ermenek and Marash, and the longer coast

ledger.note: Page silent on the year: Leo 'conquered Isauria and came as far as [Iconium]' and 'doubled its Mediterranean coast' (Cilicia page), all after 1187 and undated; the year is Cliopatria's. The Leo I page also has him taking Heraclea and giving it up for a large ransom.

6 January 1198: Leo is crowned king, and the principality becomes a kingdom. 'Leo was crowned on 6 January 1198 (or 1199)' at Tarsus; the Cilicia page gives 1198 and says the crown came with a banner in the name of Henry VI.
c. 1204: Leo seizes Antiochene fortresses in the Amanus after Renoart's rebellion; 'His 1205 siege of Trapessac (25 December) failed'. The page gives 'around 1204' and no list of places.

14 February 1216: Leo enters Antioch. 'Leo ... entered it during the night of 14 February 1216, and the Templars surrendered the citadel within days', for his candidate Raymond-Roupen; Kaykaus I took Armenian forts north of the Taurus meanwhile.
1219: Bohemond IV regains Antioch. 'Bohemond IV regained Antioch after a revolt led by William Farabel invited him back'; Raymond-Roupen fled to Cilicia and Leo died in May 1219.

14 June 1226: the Hethumids join the Rubenids on the throne. 'On June 14, 1226, Constantine forced Isabella to marry his own son, Hethum', making them co-rulers; the Rubenid house gives way to the Hethumids within the same state.

region.text: the far-west coast and the northern castles outside the 1260 shape

ledger.note: Page silent on the year: Karaman Bey's conquests of the 1240s 'were mainly at the expense of Lesser Armenia' (Karamanids page, with Larende and Ermenek given c. 1260); Cliopatria draws the loss in 1260. Gaban and Hajin are inside the removed area although the Cilicia page keeps them Armenian to 1375.
Page silent on the year: 'Marash and Behesni were recovered in the 1250s' (Cilicia page, decade only); Cliopatria's 1260 shape reaches 38.2 E.

c. 1260: Mut and Ermenek pass to the Karamanids. 'c. 1260: Kilij Arslan IV gave Karaman Bey Larende and Ermenek'; the infobox dates the Battle of Mut to 1260. The page says the Seljuk gave the lands, so the Armenian share is the reading of the earlier conquests.
1342: Guy de Lusignan is anointed as Constantine II after Levon IV's assassination in 1341; the Hethumids give way to the Lusignans within the same state.

region.text: Adana and Tarsus and the plain

ledger.note: 1359: the Mamluks take Adana and Tarsus. 'The Mamluk army took over Adana and Tarsus, two major cities of the plain, leaving few castles to the Armenians.'

region.text: Sis and the remaining Armenian castles

ledger.note: 13 April 1375: Sis falls to the Mamluks; Gaban follows. 'The Mamluks gained control of the remaining areas of Cilicia, thus ending three centuries of Armenian rule' (Ramadanids page); Leo V fled to Castile.
13 April 1375: the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia ends. 'Sis fell on April 13, and Gaban followed'; the title passed to James I of Cyprus in 1396.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of Cilicia (John II Komnenos)

zones.text: the 1111 shape plus the coastal cities Levon I integrated

wars.outcome: John II took most cities of the plains and the principality; Leo, Roupen and Thoros were captured, and Cilicia stayed Byzantine for eight years.

wars.name: Thoros II's wars with Byzantium and Antioch
wars.outcome: Thoros took Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun in 1151, faced Masud at Anazarbus in 1154 and gave up Berdus to Kilij Arslan in 1157; in 1158 he paid homage to Manuel I in a treaty.
wars.note: The Cilicia page has the homage treaty in 1158; the Thoros II page has no account of Manuel's campaign.

wars.name: Leo I's Bagras war
wars.outcome: Leo captured and kept Bagras in 1191; the 1192 peace, brokered by Henry II of Champagne, had Leo and Bohemond renounce suzerainty claims and left Bagras with Leo.

wars.name: War of the Antiochene Succession
wars.outcome: Leo seized Amanus fortresses around 1204, held Antioch from 14 February 1216 for Raymond-Roupen and lost it to Bohemond IV in 1219; the war 'came to a rather unspectacular end' with Leo's death in May 1219.
wars.note: Bohemond IV 'persuaded' Kaykaus I to invade Cilicia in 1208; truces of 1202, 1206 and 1212 did not hold.

wars.name: Rum conquests of Armenian forts and the vassalage of 1225
wars.outcome: Kaykaus I captured Armenian forts north of the Taurus while Leo was in Antioch; Kayqubad I's Cilicia campaign of 1225 'reduced the kingdom of Cilician Armenia to a vassal state'. The Cilicia page adds that Kayqubad took 'regions west of Seleucia'.
wars.note: The Kaykaus I page has Cilicia capturing Ereğli and Ulukışla and later being subjugated, undated and marked 'citation needed'.

wars.name: Mongol alliance and the war with Rum (1244-1259)
wars.outcome: Hethum I submitted to the Mongols after Köse Dağ (1244), sent Sempad to Karakorum in 1247, was attacked by Rum in 1245, visited Möngke in 1253-1256 and fought beside Hulagu in 1259-1260; Marash and Behesni were recovered in the 1250s.
wars.note: Köse Dağ page: 'Cilician Armenia voluntarily submitted in 1244 and received lands and fortresses as a reward.'

wars.name: Mamluk invasions of Cilicia
wars.outcome: Mari (1266): Thoros killed, Leo captured, Sis sacked and burnt, Hethum ransomed his son by conceding unnamed territory; Tarsus taken in 1275; ten-year truce of 1285 with ceded fortresses and a tribute of one million dirhams a year; Hromgla sacked in 1292; Mongol-Armenian victory at Wadi al-Khazandar (23 December 1299) undone in May 1300; Homs 30 March 1303.
wars.note: The Hethum I page adds that after Mari 'Adana, Tarsus, and Ayas were assaulted'. No page says which lands were annexed. Zones empty because no page opened names the places: the Cilicia page says 'The Armenians were obligated to cede many fortresses to the Mamluks' (1285) without naming them, and Hromkla was sacked, not annexed (reviewer me-09-b).

wars.name: Mamluk conquest of the Cilician plain
wars.outcome: A Mamluk invasion in 1343-1344; in 1359 the Mamluk army took Adana and Tarsus; the Ramadanid Turkmen emirate was authorised to administer Cilicia from 1352.

wars.name: Fall of Sis
wars.outcome: Sis fell on 13 April 1375 and Gaban followed; the Mamluks took the remaining areas of Cilicia.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines are given by any page; the principality and kingdom were chains of castles and cities in the Taurus and on the Cilician plain, and their outline is approximate throughout. The Bagras border is the only one the pages fix by name (the 1192 peace).

sources.title: Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia
sources.note: Identity, capitals, infobox area (about 40,000 km2 in the 13th century), Levon I's coast, the 1137 conquest, Mongol alliance, Mamluk invasions and 1375. Its ruler table is incomplete and was not used.

sources.title: Leo I, King of Armenia
sources.note: 1187 accession, undated Isauria conquests, coronation 6 January 1198 (or 1199).

sources.title: Hethum I
sources.note: 1226 marriage, Mongol submission 1244, Rum attack 1245, Mari 1266; no named lands.

sources.title: Thoros II, Prince of Armenia
sources.note: 1137 conquest and the eight years of Byzantine rule, 1141 release, 1151 Mamistra and Tel Hamdoun, 1157 Berdus.

sources.title: Ramadanids
sources.note: 1352 Ramazan Beg, 1359 Adana and Tarsus, 1375 the remaining Cilicia; no date for Ayas in 1337.

sources.title: Karamanids
sources.note: Karamanid conquests at the expense of Lesser Armenia in the 1240s, c. 1260 Larende and Ermenek, Konya 1277.

sources.title: Kayqubad I
sources.note: The 1225 Cilicia campaign and vassalage (opened for the Rum dossier).

sources.title: Battle of Köse Dağ
sources.note: Cilician Armenia's voluntary submission to the Mongols in 1244 (opened for the Rum dossier).

notes: Page budget 9 of 9 used (seven opened for this state, two shared with the Rum dossier). No rulers are given: the Cilicia page's table has missing end dates and the Hethum I page disagrees (abdication 1269 against 1270). Unsettled: (1) Capitals: the infobox has Tarsus 1080-1198 and Sis 1198-1375, the body has Thoros I moving the seat to Sis around 1100; the body is followed because Cliopatria's 1099-1146 shapes do not include Tarsus. (2) The west: the Cilicia page has Kayqubad I taking 'regions west of Seleucia' (undated), the Rum page has Cilicia taking the coast from Rum in the 1240s, the Karamanids page has Karaman Bey taking Lesser Armenian land in the 1240s and Larende/Ermenek from the Seljuks c. 1260; the 1192-1259 shape's reach to 30.6 E is unverified and the Rum dossier has Alanya Rum's from 1221. (3) 1260-1304: Cliopatria's shape drops Gaban and Hajin though the Cilicia page keeps them to 1375 (the shape was not repaired for lack of coordinates a page gives). (4) Mamluk tribute and cessions after Mari (1266) and the truce of 1285 are unnamed by the pages; the mamluk-sultanate dossier should record any vassal_start and the lands. (5) Dates not found on any page: Ayas to the Mamluks (1337), Hromgla's annexation, Cyzistra (1112, unlocated), Silifke's loss between 1344 and 1363, Berdus (1157), Kokison. (6) 'Vassal' relations in which Cilicia is the vassal (Byzantium from 1158, Rum 1225-1244, the Mongols from 1244, the Mamluks) belong to the suzerains' ledgers: eu-05 (byzantine-empire), ia-02 (mongol-empire, ilkhanate) and me-09 (mamluk-sultanate, sultanate-of-rum, where vassal_start/vassal_end for Cilicia 1225-1244 are written). (7) Gazetteer names needed: Mamistra (Misis), Tel Hamdoun (Toprakkale), Bagras (Baghras), Vahka (Feke), Sis (Kozan), Hromgla (Rumkale), Silifke, Mut, Ermenek, Amanus, Isauria; coordinates used.
